chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who missed the ghusl on Friday. He said: “He performs ghusl in the time between that and the night; and if he misses it, he performs ghusl on Saturday.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: the ghusl of iḥrām for hajj is also a sunnah (prophetic tradition), without disagreement; and likewise, the ghusl of iḥrām for ʿumrah is a sunnah. The evidence for that is what we have cited from the report from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr, from Ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, from his statement: “and when he enters into iḥrām.” Since iḥrām may be for hajj and for ʿumrah, it is established that the sunnah in both of them is ghusl. Then he said: the ghusl of the Day of al-Fiṭr and the ghusl of the Day of al-Aḍḥā are sunnah. The mentioned report indicates it, in that he said: “and the Day of al-Fiṭr and the Day of al-Aḍḥā.” Then he said: the ghusl of the Day of al-Ghadīr is sunnah. And we shall mention later, when mentioning the salat (prayer) of the Day of al-Ghadīr, that which indicates that ghusl on this day is recommended and encouraged; and upon it also is the consensus of the rightful sect, not differing concerning that. Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: the ghusl of the Day of ʿArafah is sunnah. So the hadith which we narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, includes mention of the ghusl of the Day of ʿArafah. Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: the ghusl of the first night of the month of Ramaḍān, and the ghusl of the middle night of it, and the ghusl of the night of the seventeenth of it, and the nineteenth night, and the twenty-first night, and the twenty-third night, are an emphasized sunnah. The report from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, includes mention of these ghusls, as does likewise the report narrated by al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr, from Ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام; and that also indicates it.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: the consecrated state entered for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath performed for purification on specific occasions
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an obligation
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, during which specific nights are marked for recommended ghusl
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, for which a recommended ghusl is discussed
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْغَدِيرِ: the Day of Ghadir, on which ghusl is described as recommended
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah, for which ghusl is mentioned as sunnah

ai.seo_question: Which occasions have recommended ghusl according to this hadith in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This passage discusses recommended ghusls connected to sacred times and acts of worship, including Friday, iḥrām for hajj and ʿumrah, Eid days, Ghadir, ʿArafah, and selected nights of Ramaḍān. It presents these as sunnah (prophetic tradition) or emphasized sunnah, citing transmitted reports and scholarly consensus within the Imami Shia tradition.
